task.description:
Design (do not implement) a permanent acknowledgment mechanism for tools/lint_handoffs.py so that H003 (148 BLOCKER, completed_at precedes started_at, unrecoverable), H004 (34 BLOCKER, started_at precedes created_at, unrecoverable), H005 (5 BLOCKER, status COMPLETED but completed_at unset, unrecoverable), and H009 (38 MAJOR, orphaned PENDING/IN_PROGRESS step bypassed by later COMPLETED steps in the same run, unrecoverable/real historical irregularity) stop gating the full-corpus (non --changed) exit code while remaining permanently, individually visible in the tool's output. This is ISS-0627 / GH #596, scoped down from its 292-finding remainder to this 225-finding (148+34+5+38) shared-mechanism subset only, per the same batch-cap discipline used for GH-495 (-> ISS-0624/ISS-0625, LUA-08/09/10 only) and GH-594 (-> safe-mechanical H002/H008/H010 subset only, tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py).

PRIOR ART ALREADY IN THIS REPO -- adapt, don't invent from scratch:

1. tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json + tools/lint_test_isolation.py's issue_key()/load_baseline() (lines ~313-345): a content-keyed baseline file matched on severity|code|file|line|message (the FULL message text is part of the key). This is the closest existing analog to acceptance-criterion 4's requirement that a NEW, distinct H003 on a changed file must NOT match an old acknowledgment for a DIFFERENT H003 on the same file -- because lint_handoffs.py's H003/H004/H005 messages already embed the actual timestamp values (e.g. an f-string 'completed_at ({completed}) is earlier than started_at ({started})'), any change to those values changes the message and therefore the key, so a genuinely new finding cannot silently inherit an old acknowledgment. Confirm this property holds for H009's message too (it embeds len(later_completed) and run_id, so re-check whether two DIFFERENT orphan situations on the same step could ever produce byte-identical messages before relying on message-text alone; if so, consider whether the key should also fold in a stable content fingerprint component beyond severity|code|path|message, or whether the existing fields already suffice for this specific data shape).

2. tools/lint_test_wiring.py's KNOWN_UNATTACHED ledger (lines ~120-136, ~465-478): a small in-source dict reported every run as a distinct [KNOWN] bucket, explicitly excluded from the failure count, each entry required to name its tracking issue, with the comment 'EMPTY, and that is the intended steady state' establishing that a ledger is not a way to permanently silence a check -- it is a visible, still-counted register of accepted debt. This is the right precedent for the reporting/exit-code semantics (a 4th bucket alongside BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR, e.g. ACKNOWLEDGED, printed and tallied but not gating exit code), even though its dict-literal storage mechanism is too small-scale for 225 entries and should not be copied verbatim -- use the baseline-file approach (item 1) for storage at this volume instead.

3. tools/lint_test_tenant_provisioning.py's --no-baseline flag and 'Suppressed N issue(s) from baseline' print line: the CLI convention for making baseline suppression itself auditable/disableable (so the check's own effectiveness can be validated by a human or CI running --no-baseline).

4. tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json's provenance header fields: version, generated_at, source (exact command used to regenerate), regenerated_by (which run/PR), regeneration_note (free-text of what changed and why), last_line_sync. This is the right shape for the WHO/WHEN/WHY provenance CLAUDE.md and ISS-0627 ask for, but note it is FILE-LEVEL provenance (one note per regeneration of the whole file) -- ISS-0627's acceptance criteria additionally wants each of the 225 entries individually reasoned. Design whether that means (a) one shared reason per generating run recorded once in the header plus a per-category rationale, since all 225 entries share exactly 4 root causes (H003/H004/H005/H009, each already fully explained in ISS-0627's symptom field) and per-entry free-text would be repetitive noise rather than genuine distinct reasoning, or (b) truly separate per-entry reason strings. Recommend (a) unless you find a concrete reason a specific entry needs its own distinct rationale, since CLAUDE.md's own anti-pattern warning is about gates being silently weakened, not about acknowledgment text being insufficiently verbose -- but make this call explicitly and justify it in the design doc rather than silently picking one.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS (from ISS-0627 acceptance criteria + this run's diagnosis):

A. Record location: propose e.g. docs/issues/lint_handoffs_acknowledgments.json (docs/issues/ is already the registry home for issue-tracking artefacts in this repo, and this is conceptually an extension of ISS-0627's own record, not a new top-level concern) OR tools/lint_handoffs.baseline.json (matching the tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json sibling-file convention exactly, which keeps 'the linter and its baseline' colocated the way every other lint tool in this repo already does it). Recommend the tools/ sibling-file convention for consistency with the 2 existing baseline files unless you find a reason docs/issues/ is meaningfully better -- but make the choice explicit.

B. Required fields per acknowledged finding (or per header, per your A/B decision above): the file path this finding is on (matching the `file` key convention already used by lint_test_isolation.baseline.json -- not to be confused with the arbitrary `handoff_id` field inside that JSON file's own payload), the finding code (H003/H004/H005/H009), a dated timestamp from the real clock (python tools/utcnow.py, matching every other timestamp rule in CLAUDE.md -- never invented), a human-readable reason (can reference ISS-0627's already-written root-cause text rather than re-deriving 225 individual explanations), and which run/agent/script produced the acknowledgment entry (the 'who' -- e.g. run_id + tool name, matching regenerated_by/source in the existing baseline precedent).

C. Generation mechanism: NOT 225 hand-typed entries. Design a reviewed, one-time script (parallel to tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py's own existence as a reviewed script for GH-594's mechanical subset) that runs tools/lint_handoffs.py's existing detection logic (import and reuse _lint_parsed_handoff/lint_orphans, do not reimplement the predicates a second time -- reimplementation risk is exactly the kind of drift preexisting_file_finding_codes already avoids by delegating to the same functions) and mechanically emits one baseline entry per CURRENTLY-EXISTING H003/H004/H005/H009 finding, with the header carrying the single shared generation record (timestamp, source command, run_id, and a reference to ISS-0627/GH-596 for the shared rationale). Human/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR review happens once, on the generating script and its dry-run output diff -- not on 225 individual entries.

D. lint_handoffs.py full-corpus integration: findings whose severity|code|path|message key matches a baseline entry move from their normal BLOCKER/MAJOR bucket into a 4th ACKNOWLEDGED bucket -- still individually printed (e.g. prefixed '[ACKNOWLEDGED]' the way lint_test_wiring.py prefixes '[KNOWN]'), still individually counted in a distinct tally, but excluded from the counts['BLOCKER'] or counts['MAJOR'] check at the bottom of main(). This must apply ONLY to the full-corpus path -- --changed mode already has its own, separate, orthogonal pre-existing-finding-diff mechanism (preexisting_file_finding_codes / preexisting_run_finding_codes, added in GH-594) that must NOT be confused with or merged into this one: --changed asks 'did THIS branch introduce this finding', the new mechanism asks 'has this specific historical finding been reviewed and accepted as permanent record'. A file can be simultaneously outside --changed's scope AND have some findings acknowledged and others not (e.g. if a future PR fixes some but not all H003s in a file already on the baseline) -- design the interaction between the two modes explicitly (recommendation: apply baseline-matching identically in both modes, since an acknowledged finding is acknowledged regardless of which mode is scanning, but --changed's own pre-existing-diff logic still runs first/independently on whatever isn't baseline-matched).

E. --no-baseline flag (mirroring tools/lint_test_tenant_provisioning.py) so the acknowledgment mechanism itself can be validated/audited by running without it.

F. A brand-new H003/H004/H005/H009 on a file NOT in the baseline (or with a message that doesn't match any baseline entry for that file+code) must report as normal BLOCKER/MAJOR -- verify this is the natural consequence of exact message-text matching (it is, per the analysis above) and state that explicitly as a verified property in the design doc, with a worked example (e.g. show that editing a handoff's started_at to fix an unrelated H004 would, if it accidentally introduced a new H003, produce a message with different timestamp values than any baseline entry, and therefore report as new).

OUT OF SCOPE for this design (tracked in ISS-0627 for future runs, do not design or implement here): H013 (needs an explicit policy decision on whether whole-hour-offset correction clears the no-judgment bar -- may end up folded into this same baseline mechanism per ISS-0627's own acceptance criteria, but that decision is deferred to H013's own run, which should re-read this run's design once it exists rather than duplicating it), H001-structural (~4 files, per-file delimiter judgment), H006-CONDITIONAL (1 finding, needs the file's own context read by hand), H007 (69 findings/~10 files, schema-migration decision). Do not touch tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py's existing scope.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc under src/design/ names the baseline record's exact file location and full JSON schema (header provenance fields + per-finding entry fields), with explicit justification of the docs/issues/ vs tools/ sibling-file location choice

Design explicitly reuses tools/lint_handoffs.py's existing detection functions (_lint_parsed_handoff, lint_orphans) for the one-time generation script rather than reimplementing the H003/H004/H005/H009 predicates a second time

Design specifies the exact key-matching scheme (severity|code|path|message or documented variant) and includes a worked example showing a brand-new distinct finding on the same file does NOT match an old baseline entry

Design specifies the new ACKNOWLEDGED bucket's exact interaction with lint_handoffs.py's exit-code logic (excluded from BLOCKER/MAJOR count) and print output (individually listed, e.g. '[ACKNOWLEDGED]' prefix)
Design specifies the --no-baseline flag and its printed 'Suppressed N' or equivalent audit line

Design explicitly states how this baseline mechanism composes with (and stays distinct from) --changed mode's existing preexisting_file_finding_codes/preexisting_run_finding_codes diff logic from GH-594 -- these are two different questions and must not be merged into one
Design covers all 4 categories (H003, H004, H005, H009) -- not a subset
Design does not touch or redesign tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py's existing safe-mechanical scope (H002/H008/H010/H006-partial/H001-encoding)
Design explicitly excludes H013/H001-structural/H006-CONDITIONAL/H007 from this run's scope, consistent with ISS-0627
No implementation code written in this step -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 2b) reviews the design before BACKEND-DEV (Step 3) implements it

result.summary: Designed a permanent acknowledgment (baseline) mechanism for tools/lint_handoffs.py covering H003 (148 BLOCKER), H004 (34 BLOCKER), H005 (5 BLOCKER), and H009 (38 MAJOR) -- 225 findings total. Resolved the H009 collision question raised in the handoff: the message text `f"status is {status} but {len(later_completed)} later step(s) in run {run_id} are COMPLETED..."` embeds a COUNT of later-completed steps, not their identities, so two genuinely different orphan situations on the same file CAN produce a byte-identical message if the count happens to coincide after the run directory's file membership changes (confirmed this is a real risk, not hypothetical, by checking git history: handoff step files have been deleted/added/reorganized within run directories over the corpus's life). H003/H004/H005 were confirmed safe under plain severity|code|path|message matching (their messages embed the actual differing values, or in H005's case the predicate is binary with no room for a same-message-different-finding case). Fixed the H009 key by folding in a sorted fingerprint of later_completed's actual file paths as an extra key component (H009 only), with a worked example proving the fix. Recommended baseline location: tools/lint_handoffs.baseline.json (tools/ sibling-file convention matching the 2 existing baselines), not docs/issues/, with explicit justification. Schema: file-level header provenance (version/generated_at/source/regenerated_by/regeneration_note) plus a shared reasons map keyed by code (H003/H004/H005/H009, referencing ISS-0627's already-written root-cause text) plus per-finding entries (file/code/matching_key/reason_ref/acknowledged_at/acknowledged_by) -- decided ONE shared reason per category rather than 225 individual free-text reasons, justified explicitly (all 225 share exactly 4 root causes; per-entry text would be repetitive noise or fabricated distinctiveness). Generation mechanism is a new one-time reviewed script (tools/generate_lint_handoffs_baseline.py) that imports and reuses lint_handoffs.py's own _lint_parsed_handoff and lint_orphans rather than reimplementing predicates, with a differential selftest proving its local H009 orphan-walk copy stays byte-identical to lint_orphans's real output. Design specifies the new ACKNOWLEDGED bucket (excluded from counts['BLOCKER']/counts['MAJOR'] gating, individually printed with [ACKNOWLEDGED] prefix per lint_test_wiring.py's [KNOWN] precedent), the --no-baseline flag mirroring lint_test_tenant_provisioning.py plus its audit print line, and explicitly how this composes with --changed mode's existing preexisting_file_finding_codes/preexisting_run_finding_codes (GH-594): baseline-matching applies identically in both modes, running after --changed's own pre-existing-diff filtering, as two independent gates in series -- not merged into one mechanism. Includes 5 mutation-checkable test specs (TS-BASELINE-01 through 05) covering: baseline-matched finding excluded from gating but still printed; brand-new finding on an already-baselined file not excluded; the H009 collision scenario specifically disambiguated; --no-baseline restores full gating; generation script's H009 capture logic differentially matches lint_orphans. Does not touch tools/repair_handoff_bookkeeping.py's GH-594 scope. Explicitly excludes H013/H001-structural/H006-CONDITIONAL/H007 with a coverage-confirmation section. No implementation code written -- all code blocks are illustrative signatures/formulas per Type E convention. tools/lint_design_artefact.py src/design/iss0627-lint-handoffs-acknowledgment.md exits 0 (OK, no issues).
